title: Latency guardrail rollout calendar and release notes draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document is a working draft describing a short‑window rollout for the December release whose primary risk vector is latency regression. It combines a compact rollout calendar, preflight + smoke checklists focused on percentile latency & token throughput, and a customer/engineering release notes draft.

Goals:
- Ship model routing and batching improvements with bounded latency impact
- Detect regressions at 95th/99th percentile before broad exposure
- Provide clear rollback/mitigation thresholds tied to telemetry queries
- Produce concise release notes for internal and external audiences

Assumptions and constraints:
- Target environments: hosted API region-us-central and Dedicated GPU pools (dc-us-west-2).
- Traffic shaping will be used during canary windows (rate limit to 20% of baseline QPS).
- Observability: metrics via telemetry service (latency_ms_{p50,p95,p99}, error_rate, request_rate) and traces for sample requests.

High-level rollout calendar (one-week plan):
- Day -3 (2026-12-03): Finalize canary config, pin model variant, prepare PR and infra knobs. Owner: Priya.
- Day -1 (2026-12-05): Dry-run in staging: run noise-injection and load profile. Nightly smoke to be green. Owner: SRE shift.
- Day 0 (2026-12-06 morning): Canary launch — 5% traffic to new path for 60 minutes. Telemetry sampling rate: 100%.
- Day 0 (2026-12-06 midday): If green, expand to 20% for 3 hours; run full smoke matrix.
- Day 0 (2026-12-06 evening): Expand to 50% if stable. Begin 4-hour observation window at 50%.
- Day +1 (2026-12-07): Expand to 100% in host region-us-central if no triggers. Schedule Dedicated fleet gradual ramp next week.
- Day +3 to +7 (2026-12-09 to 2026-12-13): Dedicated capacity ramp: 10 -> 50 -> 100% (each step 24h) with telemetry checks between steps.

Preflight checklist (must be completed before Day -1):
- [ ] Merge PR and produce immutable release tag (runtime v2.34.0).
- [ ] Bake container into the snapshot registry and verify checksum.
- [ ] Canary config: rate limits, sampling rate, roll-forward/rollback flags added to the feature-flag service.
- [ ] Confirm per-route dashboards are live & links posted to the release Slack channel.
- [ ] Create smoke datasets: short convo (latency-sensitive) and long-seq (throughput-sensitive).
- [ ] Update runbook pointers for SRE and on-call; assign release commander & escalation path.

Smoke test matrix (execute at each traffic-update step):
- Latency sweep: p50, p95, p99 for both short and long sequences (baseline vs canary).
- Token-throughput: tokens/sec comparison and CPU/GPU utilization snapshots.
- Error surface: 4xx/5xx counts, rate-limited responses, timeouts.
- Model quality sanity: basic sample prompts for hallucination/format regressions (quick human review).
- Trace checks: ensure no new long tail (>5s) trace spans introduced.

Telemetry queries (templates for quick copy):
- p99 latency delta: sum(last_5m(latency_ms_p99{env:prod,route:/generate})) - sum(baseline_p99) / baseline_p99*100
- error rate: rate(requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) / rate(requests_total[5m])
- cold start rate: increase in first-byte latency for pooled instances
(Translate to our metrics DSL in the incident channel).

Guardrails and automatic triggers (if any trigger fires, pause and investigate; automatic rollback optional):
- Severity A (immediate rollback recommended):
  - p99 latency increases >25% vs baseline for 5 consecutive 5m windows AND absolute p99 >1200ms
  - error rate increases >1% absolute AND error rate doubles baseline
- Severity B (investigate, hold expansion):
  - p95 latency increases 15–25%
  - CPU/GPU saturation >85% sustained for 10m
  - Trace tail shows new span >3s in critical path for >1% of requests
- Severity C (operational notes):
  - minor regressions in p50 or sporadic 5xx spikes under 0.5%

Immediate mitigation checklist (first 30 minutes):
- Notify release Slack channel with telemetry snapshot.
- Roll traffic back to previous variant (feature-flag toggle).
- If rollback fails: scale up safe pool or route to secondary region.
- Collect flamegraphs and top traces; escalate to runtime on-call.

Rollback playbook (linear steps):
1) Flip feature flag to previous variant (automated, should take <60s).
2) If flip incomplete: revert canary service in orchestration console and redeploy previous tag.
3) If redeploy blocked: promote emergency scaling / activate fallback routing to model-legacy.
4) Post-rollback: run for 30m steady-state observation, capture full telemetry, create an RCA ticket.

Roles and contact list:
- Release commander: Priya Natarajan (pager: paged via rotation)
- SRE lead (canary ops): Elliot Park
- Runtime lead (debug/PR): Luis Alvarez
- Observability/Telemetry: Maya Chen
- Customer comms draft review: Zoë Martin

Post-release validation (Day +1 to +7):
- Daily checks for first week: p99, errors, user-reported anomalies; keep a high-sample trace capture for 24–48h.
- Quality regression set: run a 2000-prompt eval set through canary vs baseline and report delta on rouge/bleu-like metrics and hallucination keywords.

Customer-facing release notes (draft):
Title: Faster, more efficient inference routing (Dec 2026)
Short blurb: Today we’re rolling out an improvement to inference routing and batching that reduces overhead for many short-turn conversations while preserving accuracy. Most customers will see lower median latency and improved throughput for bursty traffic.
Technical highlights (for customers comfortable with ops):
- Optimized batching for small requests that reduces median latency on short prompts by ~10–20% in our hosted regions.
- Improved fallback routing logic to reduce time-to-first-token when a pool is saturated.
- No changes required to your integration; behavior is backward compatible.
Note to enterprise customers: If you pin model variants or use private deployments with strict latency SLOs, contact support before the week of Dec 6 if you want a manually coordinated rollout.

Internal release notes (engineering summary):
- Runtime v2.34.0: batching/routing heuristics + telemetry labels + FF guardrail hooks.
- Config changes: route/routing-policy v1.7; canary flag release.experimental.routing_v2; orchestration policy updated to allow staged scaling.
- Migration steps: none for persisted KV; cache key format unchanged.
- Known issues: rare tail-of-session latency increase observed in internal perf tests when concurrency > 6000; mitigation available via throttle config.

Open questions / items to resolve in doc before final:
- Decide whether automated rollback should be permitted at Severity A or require manual confirmation by release commander.
- Final acceptance thresholds for Dedicated pool ramp (currently conservative).
- Human-review cadence for model-quality sanity checks during canary (who signs off?).

Quick action items (next 48h):
- Elliot: wire up sample-trace collection to the release Slack channel (due 2026-11-29).
- Maya: publish the per-route dashboard snapshot link and add short playbook notes (due 2026-11-30).
- Luis: prepare a debug script that captures top 100 slow traces and associated model inputs (due 2026-11-30).
- Zoë: prepare customer-facing blurb and two short enterprise templates for coordinated rollouts (due 2026-12-01).

Appendix: example Slack notification template (copyable)
[RELEASE-COMMANDER] Canary 5% started for routing_v2 in us-central — monitoring p50/p95/p99, errors. Links: dashboard /runbook /trace-sample. Expected check-in at +60m.

---
Document history: v0.1 created 2026-11-20 by Priya Natarajan; working edits 2026-11-24 to 2026-11-28.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally concise — prefer explicit numeric guardrails and stepwise expansion. Add any missing telemetry queries or circuit-breaker knobs you want enforced by automation.
